# 2 Baruch Chapter 11 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 11:1 — "no one knew of me"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "and-no-one-knew-of-me" | Literal Syriac idiom of concealment |
| LOGOS | "and no one knew of me" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "Nobody knew I was there" | Paraphrase — explicit location |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "No one knew of me" is the Syriac idiom for being hidden/unknown, which is broader than merely spatial. Baruch's prophetic hiddenness is a significant theme.

---

## 11:4 — "multitude of your mercies"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-multitude-of-thy-mercies" | Literal construct chain |
| LOGOS | "the multitude of your mercies" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "all your compassion" | "Compassion" (singular) for "mercies" (plural); "all" for "multitude" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Multitude of mercies" (rov rachamim) is a fixed liturgical phrase in Syriac and Hebrew prayer. The plural "mercies" carries the covenantal weight of repeated divine acts; "compassion" is too abstract.

---

## 11:7 — "Have you indeed set your heart on..."

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Hast-thou-indeed-set-thy-heart on-all-these-things" | Archaic formal literal |
| LOGOS | "Have you indeed set your heart on all these things" | Formal modern English |
| PNEUMA | "have you really let all that has happened...get into your heart" | Inverted idiom; adds "really" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Set your heart on" is the standard idiom for deep concern. PNEUMA's inversion ("get into your heart") loses the active volitional sense — Baruch is being asked whether he has given his heart over to grief as a choice.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 3**
